source: Onkelos on Exod 27:9; the lash row at Mishnah Makkot 3:3 (read in the backfill exam)
claim_en: THE COURT'S HANGINGS ARE A LEGAL BOUNDARY. The kelaim (hangings, rendered SERADIN) enclose the courtyard — and the case shelf uses that fixture as a statute's line: most-holy offerings eaten 'outside the CURTAINS' is a forty-lashes row (Mishnah Makkot 3:3 — read in full in this morning's backfill exam; credited, not re-read). The fence itself becomes the offense's definition.

source: Onkelos on Exod 27:18; the measure row at Mishnah Eruvin 2:5
claim_en: THE COURT BECOMES A UNIT OF MEASURE. A hundred cubits by fifty (chamshin be-chamshin) — and the tradition takes THIS enclosure as its standard area: bet satayim ('the space of two seah'), the Sabbath-carrying limit for any enclosure, is defined 'like the courtyard of the tabernacle' (Mishnah Eruvin 2:5). Every karpef in Sabbath law is measured against this verse.

source: Onkelos on Exod 27:20; the oil-grades row at Mishnah Menachot 8:5
claim_en: CRUSHED FOR THE LIGHT — THE GRADE IS SCOPED. mishcha zeta dakhya KATISHA le-anhara ('PURE olive oil, CRUSHED, for the light') — the stricter crushed-grade demanded for the LAMP only: katit la-maor ve-lo katit la-menachot ('crushed for the light, not crushed for the meal-offerings') — the case row Mishnah Menachot 8:5. The tadir-token again ('continually'). In-span note: 27:20-21 opens the next portion; the unit is read whole.

source: Onkelos on Exod 27:21 (+ the ash-duty at 27:3)
claim_en: THE PRIESTHOOD'S FIRST STANDING ASSIGNMENT, GIVEN BEFORE THE PRIESTHOOD. Aaron and his sons order the lamp me-ramsha ad tzafra ('from EVENING to MORNING') before the LORD — chukat olam rendered KEYAM ALAM ('an EVERLASTING STATUTE') le-darehon ('for their generations'): the parashah closes on a perpetual duty assigned before its bearers are even clothed (that is the next portion). The dawn side of the cycle already named at 27:3: le-misfei kitmei ('to REMOVE its ashes') — the ash-clearance in the vessel list.

A RECORDED ENGINEERING OBJECTION AT THE SPEC, WITH ITS ANSWER STACK. Moses: wood plated bronze under a PERPETUAL FIRE (Leviticus 6:6) — the fire will pass the plating and burn the wood. The answer: My measures are not yours (fire-angels under water-firmaments — He makes peace in His heights), and the precedents — dead things enter before Me and leave alive (Aaron's staff; Solomon's fruiting cedars), Moses himself walked into the fire (our 20:21 quoted back). R. Nechemiah's datum: plating a DINAR'S thickness. Reason-layer: bronze atones for the brazen forehead. The acrostic and measure correspondences of Tanchuma 10 ride as the letter-arithmetic family.

source: Mishnah Eruvin 10:15 + Mishnah Tamid 5:5 (Step 9 Terumah exam)
claim_en: THE ASH-POT'S SECOND SERVICE. Our 27:3's pots-for-ashes have a case-side face: the great bronze psakhter (its services listed at Mishnah Tamid 5:5) is overturned over a dead creeping thing found in the sanctuary (Mishnah Eruvin 10:15), where the removal disputes run — belt vs wooden tongs (impurity must not linger vs must not spread), and the zones bounded by cut-off liability (R. Shimon ben Nannas vs R. Akiva). The altar vessel running in purity law.

source: Midrash Tanchuma, Tetzaveh 2 + 3 + 4 (the lamp sections at this unit's 27:20-21; Tetzaveh sitting)
claim_en: THE LIGHT FLOWS OUTWARD — THE NOT-NEED ARCHITECTURE. The spine argues from the building itself that the lamp is granted, not needed: the menorah stands OUTSIDE the veil, at the table's RIGHT where kings keep their lamp at the left (26:35's stations running as proof), and the Temple windows are inverted — narrow within, wide without — the light leaving the house to the world. R. Chanina segan ha-kohanim's first-person Temple testimony rides: the lamp lit at the year's head burned the whole year; Jerusalem's courtyards used its light. The command as participation grant (Job 14:15's desire-for-the-work-of-Your-hands frame).
